transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-08-03
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Carlos Ruiz (Redwood SE), Sofia Lin (Tidewave Head of Platform), Derek Moore (Tidewave Senior Backend Engineer), Priya Shah (Tidewave Security Architect)

Summary: quick discovery focused on integration surface area \u0014 SDKs, orchestration with LangChain/LlamaIndex, how to put Redwood behind an internal gateway/proxy, practical rate limits/quotas per route, and observability hooks for tracing/cost.

Topics:
- Integration paths: direct SDK, LangChain/LlamaIndex, HTTP gateway
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs for throughput/latency/data residency
- Rate limiting & quotas (per-route, per-team, burst policies)
- Observability: token-level cost breakdown, traces, per-model dashboards
- Security: VPC/Private, SSO, KMS, audit logs

Transcript body:
00:00 Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood, and with me is Carlos Ruiz our SE, we'll do a quick run through your integration surface and then focus on the parts you flagged \u0014 Lang Chain integration, gateway and rate limits.
00:12 Sofia: hey thanks, excited to chat; we want to understand where Redwood fits in our infra and how much work to wire it to our gateway and observability stack.
00:20 Carlos: great, quick high level \u0014 Redwood supports hosted API calls, dedicated reserved pools, and a private deployment model. From integration point of view we have SDKs for Python and Node, a REST API, and reference connectors for LangChain and LlamaIndex. Those connectors are maintained in our examples repo (link shared in chat).
00:38 Derek: can you share the repo link? we use LangChain heavily, and our ingestion pipeline is built on top of LlamaIndex for some retrieval ops.
00:44 Carlos: absolutely \u0014 we typically point teams to the LangChain examples (python and node) and a LlamaIndex adapter; they're lightweight wrappers over the HTTP/streaming endpoints. We'll drop the links.
00:58 Priya: couple security Qs up front \u0014 for Dedicated or Private, do you support VPC peering and customer-managed KMS? and what does audit logging look like?
01:10 Maya: yes on both \u0014 Dedicated can be deployed in customer VPCs in our private offering, and we integrate with KMS/HSM for key management in Private. Audit logs are available by route and include request metadata, model used, and basic token counts; for enterprise we provide longer retention as an add-on. Carlos will follow up with the SOC2/ISO docs.
01:29 Derek: when you say "audit logs include token counts" is that token-level cost or just coarse metrics? we need per-customer token billing granularity.
01:36 Carlos: we provide token-level cost breakdowns in the Redwood Console and via logs. It's not necessarily every token payload in the wire logs, but we emit tokens consumed per request with model identifier and route id. That lets you reconstruct cost per tenant.
01:50 Sofia: good. On the network side, we have an internal envoy gateway; we prefer not to let services talk directly to external APIs. Can Redwood be placed behind our gateway/proxy?
02:01 Carlos: yes, we see two common patterns: 1) services call Redwood directly using the SDKs with mTLS and VPC egress rules; 2) route everything through your internal gateway \u0014 we recommend putting Redwood credentials into a secrets store and using per-service tokens. If using hosted, you'll open egress to Redwood endpoints; for Dedicated/Private we can keep traffic within the VPC. Note: if you use a gateway with request buffering, watch streaming behaviour \u0014 envoy can buffer, impacting real-time streams.
02:32 Derek: buffering is fine for batch ops, but we do some low-latency chat features where streaming is important. Are there any known issues with streaming through proxies?
02:41 Carlos: streaming works but you need to avoid proxies that fully buffer the response. Configure passthrough for chunked transfers or gRPC streams. Our SDKs support streaming with a small client-side buffer and reconnect handling.
02:55 Maya: on quotas \u0014 we expose per-api-key rate limits and per-route quotas. Enterprise tiers can have dedicated pools with reserved throughput and bursting rules. Typical config: per-route rps, per-account monthly token quota, and emergency circuit-breakers.
03:10 Sofia: can quotas be dynamically adjusted by route? e.g., we want a high-priority fraud model to have guaranteed QPS while less critical routes get best-effort.
03:18 Carlos: yes \u0014 routing and quotas are configurable. For Dedicated you map routes to GPU pools and set guaranteed concurrency/throughput. You can do weighted routing so critical routes hit the fast pool and others are lower priority.
03:30 Derek: what's the developer UX for that config? is it all console or API-driven?
03:35 Carlos: both \u0014 Console has per-route dashboards and quick config UIs, and everything is backed by our management API so infra teams can automate it.
03:42 Priya: about LangChain \u0014 do you provide first-class connectors or do we need to maintain our own adapters? We want as little glue code as possible.
03:51 Carlos: we maintain community examples and official connectors for common LangChain LLM wrappers and for LlamaIndex. They handle tokenization, streaming, and prompt templates. Most customers fork the example and add minimal adapters for auth and metrics.
04:05 Derek: how do you handle embeddings + vector stores? our pipeline builds embeddings and stores in an internal Milvus cluster. Any gotchas?
04:12 Carlos: embeddings are standard \u0014 you call the embeddings endpoint, get vectors and then push to your vector DB. We recommend batching and async pipelines. For high throughput we suggest using Dedicated pools to reduce latency and request contention.
04:24 Sofia: performance: our 95th latency target for chat is under 400ms for short prompts; token sizes avg ~120 tokens. Can Dedicated meet that?
04:33 Carlos: yes, with the right model and GPU profile. We'll propose a benchmark \u0014 typically small-seq chat on quantized models on A100 or H100 can hit sub-200ms p50 and p95 around your target depending on concurrency. We'll run a PoC with your traffic shape.
04:50 Maya: we'll need Derek to share request distribution and concurrency numbers; Carlos will prepare a benchmark playbook.
05:00 Priya: around compliance \u0014 do you have SOC 2 reports and do you support SAML/SSO for user access to Console?
05:07 Maya: yes SOC 2 and ISO, SAML/SSO and RBAC are supported; for Private you can map to your identity provider. We'll attach the compliance pack.
05:18 Sofia: are there any limits on model variants? we might want multiple model sizes for cost/quality tradeoffs and automatic routing.
05:25 Carlos: we support model variants and automated fallback policies; you can define routing policies by latency, cost, and fallback chains. This is how we do graceful degradation (e.g. fallback to a cheaper quantized model on overload).
05:37 Derek: on observability, we already use Datadog and Jaeger \u0014 can we get traces and per-request tags into our systems?
05:44 Carlos: yes \u0014 we have tracing hooks and emit spans that include request id, model id, and route. We also provide per-route metrics (latency, token count, errors) via Prometheus endpoints or push to your metrics backend. Logs and trace samplings are configurable.
05:58 Maya: quick note \u0014 some transcriptions in our internal docs sometimes call it "Redwood Dedicate", ignore that, it's Redwood Dedicated. (small laugh)
06:06 Sofia: ha noted.
06:10 Derek: one small practical: our developer stack uses LangChain layers. If we use your SDKs, do we need to rewrite a lot of our chain code?
06:18 Carlos: usually minimal. LangChain has a standardized LLM interface so the adapter translates calls to our SDK. You might change auth + streaming handling but most prompt and chain logic stays. We also have a short example showing how to swap a provider in under an hour.
06:32 Priya: network security: if we do hosted, what's the expected egress surface? we can't allow open egress from critical subnets.
06:40 Maya: for hosted you'll need to allow egress to Redwood endpoints (we'll provide IP ranges and DNS names). For Dedicated we can do private peering so traffic never leaves your VPC. Private on-prem is available if you need an air-gapped option.
06:55 Sofia: what's the typical timeline for a Dedicated setup? we might be time-sensitive.
07:02 Carlos: Dedicated provisioning is typically 4\u20136 weeks once contract and infra details are confirmed; Private on-prem varies more. Hosted is obviously immediate. For PoC benchmarking we can usually get you a sandbox API key in 24\u201348 hours.
07:20 Derek: a few edge cases \u0014 how do you handle long-running generation with KV cache? we have retrieval-augmented generation where context windows are large.
07:28 Carlos: our runtime handles KV caching and we expose options to persist KV cache across related requests to save compute. For very long contexts we recommend retrieval + chunking and using embeddings to narrow the context. We'll include notes in the benchmark playbook.
07:44 Sofia: curious about pricing \u0014 are embeddings priced differently and is there a separate charge for Dedicated GPUs?
07:50 Maya: embeddings are priced per 1k tokens similarly but often billed separately; Dedicated is a reserved capacity contract so pricing is a combination of reserved pool cost + per-token or per-request units depending on the plan. We'll share a breakdown spreadsheet.
08:05 Derek: any gotchas with LlamaIndex? we keep running into off-by-one tokenization with different tokenizers.
08:13 Carlos: tokenizer mismatches are common \u0014 our connectors include consistent tokenization helpers; we recommend standardizing on the same tokenizer library across pipeline and evaluation. We'll put a note and example in the LangChain/LlamaIndex doc.
08:28 Maya: time check \u0014 we're in the weeds \u0014 quick recap and next steps?
08:33 Sofia: yes please.
08:35 Maya: recap: 1) Redwood supports SDKs (Python/Node), REST/streaming endpoints, LangChain and LlamaIndex connectors; 2) Gateway/proxy is supported but avoid full-response buffering for streaming; 3) Quotas/routing configurable per-route, Dedicated supports reserved throughput; 4) Observability integrations for traces/metrics/logs and token-level cost; 5) Security: SOC2/ISO, SAML, VPC/KMS options.
08:57 Carlos: action items we agreed \u0014 I'll share benchmark checklist and sample scripts; Maya will send the compliance pack and pricing spreadsheet; Sofia will share traffic profile; we'll schedule PoC next week.
09:12 Derek: sounds good, please include a note about streaming through envoy and sample config.
09:18 Priya: and add details about KMS integration flows and audit log retention options.
09:25 Maya: will do. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with links and schedule.
09:30 Sofia: thanks, talk soon.

Notes / links mentioned in chat: LangChain examples repo (link), LlamaIndex adapter (link), benchmark playbook (to be shared), compliance pack (SOC2/ISO).

End of transcript.
